body: It looks like that ```com.arjuna.ats.internal.arjuna.utils.SocketProcessId``` should be added in the ReflectiveClass. Also the other classes which implement the ```com.arjuna.ats.arjuna.utils.Process``` interface should be added.

The default [Process implementation](https://github.com/jbosstm/narayana/blob/master/ArjunaCore/arjuna/classes/com/arjuna/ats/arjuna/utils/Process.java#L41) is set to [SocketProcessId](https://github.com/jbosstm/narayana/blob/master/ArjunaCore/arjuna/classes/com/arjuna/ats/arjuna/utils/Utility.java#L379). The quarkus narayana-jta extension does not [expose this item in its config](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/tree/master/extensions/narayana-jta/runtime/src/main/java/io/quarkus/narayana/jta/runtime). So for now I think it is best to just add the SocketProcessId class as a ReflectiveClassBuildItem. We can add other Process implementations if it is ever made configurable.

I tried out Amos's suggested fix and it works great.

I tried the reproducer on the current Quarkus master (999-SNAPSHOT) and the missing class is now found. I suspect the Quarkus team have fixed it along the way.

I don't know how Quarkus performs its magic but I'd expect it is capable of finding, and allowing, implementations of an interface to be found automatically so that the extension developer does not need to tell the build step about these implementations.

Maybe @stuartwdouglas or one of the other core team members could tell us whether the runtime provides that? Stewart, the context is that Amos wrote a simple example using 1.5.2.Final and found that in native mode narayana implementations of the Process interface (see the [previous comment](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/10180#issuecomment-648776949)) are not being discovered by the runtime even though the jta extension includes them?
@mmusgrov I tried with the master (999-SNAPSHOT) and it was still failed. I think you might not remove the fix and rebuild the narayana-jta extension ?

I tried it using the latest master (building quarkus from a fresh git clone). The steps I tried were:

```bash
# build quarkus master (999-SNAPSHOT)
git clone https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus
cd quarkus
./mvnw -Dquickly

# create a reproducer
 cd ..
 mvn io.quarkus:quarkus-maven-plugin:1.5.2.Final:create     -DprojectGroupId=org.acme     -DprojectArtifactId=getting-started     -DclassName="org.acme.getting.started.GreetingResource"     -Dpath="/hello"
 cd getting-started
 vi pom.xml # change version from 1.5.2.Final to 999-SNAPSHOT and quarkus-universe-bom to quarkus-bom

# use GRAALVM to build a native exe:
 export GRAALVM_HOME=/usr/local/graalvm-ce-java8-19.3.2
 export JAVA_HOME=${GRAALVM_HOME}
 export PATH=${GRAALVM_HOME}/bin:$PATH

 mvn -Pnative clean install

# run it
 ./target/getting-started-1.0-SNAPSHOT-runner &
 curl http://localhost:8080/hello
```

The output is "hello".

* step 2 add the narayana-jta extension
* step 3 modify the GreetingResource.java to add the ```@Transactional```
